headline: Outcry over IGP's remarks: NCP seeks removal of police chief
summary: The National Citizen Party demands the immediate removal of IGP Ali Hossain Fakir after he suggested 'crossfire' could be used if the government permits.
details: Inspector General of Police (IGP) Ali Hossain Fakir sparked widespread condemnation after stating that police would use 'crossfire' if the government allows it. The remarks were made during a bank opening event in Old Dhaka on Monday.

The National Citizen Party (NCP) has demanded the IGP's immediate removal, calling the statement a threat to the rule of law and human rights. The party argued that government approval can never legitimise extrajudicial killings.
Police Headquarters later clarified that the IGP used the term to convey firmness in law enforcement and did not mean to endorse extrajudicial killings.
The NCP accused the ruling BNP of contradicting its own pledge to end enforced disappearances and extrajudicial killings, as outlined in its 31-point state-reform plan.
The party further urged for the police force to be freed from illegal practices and called for the formation of a police commission in line with the July Charter.
caption:
Can 'crossfire' be legitimised by government approval? The NCP demands the IGP's removal after his controversial remarks.

Inspector General of Police (IGP) Ali Hossain Fakir sparked widespread condemnation after stating that police would use 'crossfire' if the government allows it. The remarks were made during a bank opening event in Old Dhaka on Monday.

The National Citizen Party (NCP) has demanded the IGP's immediate removal, calling the statement a threat to the rule of law and human rights. The party argued that government approval can never legitimise extrajudicial killings.

Police Headquarters later clarified that the IGP used the term to convey firmness in law enforcement and did not mean to endorse extrajudicial killings.

The NCP accused the ruling BNP of contradicting its own pledge to end enforced disappearances and extrajudicial killings, as outlined in its 31-point state-reform plan.

The party further urged for the police force to be freed from illegal practices and called for the formation of a police commission in line with the July Charter.

headline_marked: [[Cyclone Arnab]] forms over Bay of Bengal, to cross India as very severe storm
headline: Cyclone Arnab forms over Bay of Bengal, to cross India as very severe storm
summary: A deep depression in the Bay of Bengal has intensified into Cyclone Arnab. It is forecast to strengthen further before making landfall in India's Andhra Pradesh coast on Wednesday.
details: A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal has intensified into a cyclone named Arnab. The storm is forecast to strengthen further before crossing India's Andhra Pradesh coast as a very severe cyclonic storm on Wednesday.

As of 6:00 AM today, the cyclone was located 820 kilometres southwest of Chattogram port, 745 kilometres southwest of Cox’s Bazar port, 785 kilometres south of Mongla port and 745 kilometres south of Payra port. The maximum sustained wind speed near the centre is around 62 km/h, with gusts up to 88 km/h.

The Bangladesh Meteorological Department has asked the maritime ports of Chattogram, Cox’s Bazar, Mongla and Payra to hoist distant warning signal No 2. Fishing boats and trawlers in the North Bay of Bengal are advised to remain close to the coast and navigate with caution.

The cyclone is expected to move northwestwards and intensify into a severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal by early Tuesday morning, before crossing the Indian coast the following day.

Meteorologist Abdul Hamid Mia of the BMD stated that Cyclone Arnab is not expected to have a significant impact on Bangladesh. Coastal areas may experience light rain, with a low likelihood of heavy rainfall. Light rain may also occur in Dhaka and Rajshahi divisions after landfall.
Cyclones are classified by wind speed, with a "very severe cyclonic storm" having sustained winds of 118 to 165 km/h. Arnab is expected to reach this intensity before landfall.

Thirteen regional countries jointly name cyclones. "Arnab," meaning "sea" or "ocean," was proposed by Bangladesh and is the latest name on the sequential list used to avoid confusion when multiple storms form simultaneously.
